findings.finding: After the H1 period closed (30 Sep), CEO/64.6% holder Lord Cruddas bought ~GBP5m of shares (2-6 Oct, 604-690p) and stated in an issuer press release that the low-volatility headwind hitting peers 'is not reflected in CMC's performance' and that 'momentum remains incredibly strong', i.e. a company-level read on H1 consistent with the >=GBP550m guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance upgrade 1 Jul 2026 +41.9% (window move per baseline), FY26 prelims +16.9%, Nov 2025 interims +28.9%; Jan 2025 trading update -16.8% and Nov 2024 interims -14.8% when the line disappointed.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, so partly priced: the stock ran from 632 (2 Oct) to 716 (16 Oct) on it and has since slid back to 651 (25 Nov), below the CEO's average purchase price, so the market has given back the whole signal; if the market believed H1 tracks >=GBP550m with a possible raise, the stock would not sit 10% below its 60-day level with shorts building into the print.
findings.independence: PDMR notices on RNS (161,000 shares at 623.85p, 2 Oct; 23,011 at ~604p) https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/cmc-markets--cmcx/director-pdmr-shareholding/9806704 and Finance Magnates 7 Oct https://www.financemagnates.com/forex/analysis/low-volatility-squeezes-brokers-cmc-markets-founder-says-it-is-not-reflected-in-cmcs-performance/ (same underlying event, not independent evidence on H1).

findings.finding: IG Group guided Jul-Sep 2026 revenue ~GBP240m (-14% y/y) with OTC revenue retention ~70% against ~80% average, 'in less supportive market conditions' — the same quarter as CMC's fiscal Q2, a risk to CMC's B2C CFD income and to the quality of the half.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CMC fell 4% to 632p on 2 Oct 2026, the day of IG's update; when CMC's own retail income disappointed (Nov 2024 interims, Jan 2025 update) it fell ~15-17%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: CMC dropped 4% that day and the CEO rebutted it five days later. Kept small because it is a peer proxy, CMC says institutional/B2B is the majority of income, and a CMC-specific retention dip in its own B2C book would only show in the release.
findings.independence: CEO's own 7 Oct statement acknowledges the low-VIX backdrop for peers (https://www.cmcmarkets.com/group/press-releases/in-conversation-with-lord-peter-cruddas-cmc-markets-evolution-and-continued-growth-strategy).

findings.finding: Plus500 reported Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep) revenue $203.2m, +11% y/y, and moved FY2026 revenue/EBITDA guidance to ahead of market expectations — the retail CFD backdrop in CMC's Q2 was not uniformly weak.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No CMC-specific history on a peer read-across; CMC rose 1.5% on 26 Oct 2026 per the tape (704 from 696).
findings.why_not_priced: Peer proxy, public for a month; mostly priced, kept as a small offset to the IG read-across.

findings.finding: Matthew Lewis, head of CMC Australia & New Zealand (the region where the Westpac and ASB B2B launches sit), sold another 200,000 shares at 770p on 7 Sep 2026, inside the H1 period.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measurable reaction; stock fell from 785 (7 Sep) to 734 (9 Sep) amid general drift.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and small; a sale at a then-record price is weak evidence against the half, and is outweighed by the CEO's larger post-period purchase. Sized near zero.

outside_window.finding: Westpac white-label launch 'fully on track for an early 2027 launch' and ASB NZ go-live before end of calendar 2026 — milestones that resolve after the window unless the release re-dates them.
